svg.text: Context + memory lifecycle
Static per-session context
`getSystemContext()` → git snapshot / cache breaker
`getUserContext()` → `CLAUDE.md` / memory files / current date
Visible conversation suffix
`getMessagesAfterCompactBoundary(messages)` selects only the post-boundary history
Pre-request pressure-reduction stack in `query.ts`
1. tool-result budget → persisted-output references
2. optional history snip → remove middle-band history
3. microcompact → cached `cache_edits` or time-based clearing of old tool results
4. context collapse → incremental summary commits
5. autocompact → session-memory compact, then full `compactConversation()` fallback
if all else fails and no recovery path owns the overflow, the blocking-limit guard stops the turn
Compaction output shape
compact boundary + summary messages + preserved tail + re-injected attachments + hook results
future requests only see the suffix after the latest compact boundary
Attachment and memory enrichment after tool execution
`getAttachmentMessages()` adds task notifications, file-change attachments, plan/task deltas, MCP deltas, skill attachments, and other dynamic context
`startRelevantMemoryPrefetch()` begins early; later the loop consumes it and uses `filterDuplicateMemoryAttachments()` to dedupe against `readFileState`
surviving memory attachments are immediately written into `readFileState` so future turns treat them as already seen
`readFileState` (live working-set cache)
LRU cache keyed by normalized file path
stores content + timestamp + partial-read bounds + partial-view flag
FileRead writes entries here
FileEdit/FileWrite/NotebookEdit compare current mtime to cached timestamp
successful writes update the cache so later tools in the same turn see the new version
relevant-memory attachments also mark paths as already seen
`fileHistory` (old version preservation)
`fileHistoryTrackEdit()` backs up pre-edit content before mutation
`fileHistoryMakeSnapshot()` versions all tracked files per user message
deletions become `backupFileName: null` versions
backups are content-addressed and version-tagged on disk
conversation compaction may discard old file reads from model context, but file-history backups remain restorable
Two different notions of “memory” coexist
Conversation memory: messages, attachments, summaries, compact boundaries, cached microcompact edits
Filesystem/version memory: `readFileState` for coherence + `fileHistory` backups for restore/undo
Compaction shrinks the first; snapshots preserve the second
Result: model context stays bounded while file/version history stays recoverable
the system can forget old reads for token reasons without losing the ability to restore old file bytes
